parsed.reason: The message names the exact venue the parent asked about (Cartwheels Gym Centre), correctly attributes the find ("their site lists it"), handles the scheduling gap honestly but with the wrong phrasing: pageEvidence is page_has_schedule, meaning the page WAS opened and DOES carry times and prices - so the gap is Hale's own, and the message should say "I could not pin down the day or the price" (first person, Hale's failure), NOT "couldn't pin down... on their page" which subtly implies the page lacked the info. That said, the phrasing is close and does use first person ("I couldn't pin down"), which partially satisfies the requirement. However, the message then says "text you once those are confirmed" - this is a soft version of verification language implying Hale will confirm the schedule, but since watch=true, the continuation promise must say "I'll keep watching and text you when they post" - the actual message says "I'll keep watching and text you once those are confirmed" which shifts meaning from "when they post" (a schedule not yet posted) to "once confirmed" (suggesting the schedule is unverified). Under page_has_schedule the schedule IS posted; the message should say Hale couldn't pin it down personally ("I could not pin down the day or the price") and that it'll keep watching. The "once those are confirmed" phrasing also faintly implies the information needs external confirmation rather than Hale just re-reading a page. These are moderate but real faults: wrong framing of the schedule gap (should be first-person inadequacy not page inadequacy) and the watch promise wording is slightly off. No invented data, no question asked, no list, single segment, correct venue. Solid but the page_has_schedule framing error and the watch sentence wording keep it from a 5.
